moments.title: Silent Spring published
moments.body: Carson's book documents the ecological effects of synthetic pesticides. Chemical industry attacks the author and the science.

quote.text: The history of life on earth has been a history of interaction between living things and their surroundings.

moments.takeaway: A single book triggered structural changes in US environmental policy.

moments.title: EPA established and first Earth Day
moments.body: The first Earth Day on 22 April 1970 draws 20 million Americans. The Environmental Protection Agency is established in December.
moments.takeaway: Political pressure crystallised new federal institutions within a decade of Carson's book.

moments.title: DDT banned for agricultural use
moments.body: The agency bans most agricultural uses of DDT, citing accumulating ecological evidence.
moments.takeaway: Specific regulatory action followed from a broader public-science conversation.

now.title: Chemical regulation today
now.body: REACH (EU 2007) and analogous frameworks regulate thousands of chemicals. New concerns include PFAS, microplastics and endocrine disruptors.
now.open_questions: How should risk be assessed for chemicals in low-dose chronic exposure mixtures?

items.reflection: Environmental policy in the 20th century repeatedly hinged on writers and scientists able to translate evidence to public audiences.

moments.title: Molina and Rowland predict ozone loss
moments.who: Mario Molina and Sherwood Rowland, UC Irvine
moments.body:
The pair publish a Nature paper arguing chlorofluorocarbons could destroy stratospheric ozone.

They win the Nobel Prize in Chemistry in 1995 (with Paul Crutzen).
moments.takeaway: A theoretical prediction made years before instrumental confirmation.

moments.title: Antarctic ozone hole reported
moments.body: British Antarctic Survey scientists at Halley Bay publish data showing severe seasonal ozone depletion over Antarctica.
moments.takeaway: Patient long-term ground observations identified what satellites had filtered out.

moments.title: Montreal Protocol signed
moments.body: An international agreement phases down ozone-depleting substances. The protocol is widely cited as a model of effective environmental governance.
moments.takeaway: International cooperation produced measurable atmospheric improvement.

now.title: Stratospheric ozone today
now.body: WMO/UNEP assessments project recovery to 1980 levels around 2040 outside polar regions and 2066 over Antarctica. Unauthorised CFC-11 emissions detected in 2018 were addressed by 2021.
now.open_questions: Will geoengineering proposals (stratospheric aerosol injection) interact with ozone recovery? How robust is global compliance?

items.reflection: A relatively focused atmospheric problem with substitutable inputs produced a treaty that worked. Climate change has neither feature.

moments.title: IPCC established
moments.body:
The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change is created to assess climate science for policymakers.

The first Assessment Report (1990) summarises the evidence base.
moments.takeaway: An international scientific assessment body became central to climate policy.

moments.title: UN Framework Convention on Climate Change
moments.body: The convention establishes the framework for international climate negotiations, leading to Kyoto (1997) and Paris (2015).
moments.takeaway: Climate diplomacy operates on multi-decade negotiation timescales.

moments.title: Paris Agreement adopted
moments.body: Parties agree to hold warming below 2 C and pursue 1.5 C, with nationally determined contributions reviewed every five years.
moments.takeaway: A bottom-up architecture replaced the Kyoto top-down approach.

now.title: Climate policy today
now.body: Net-zero targets are now legislated in many jurisdictions. IPCC AR6 (2021-2023) concluded human influence on warming is unequivocal. Implementation gaps remain large.
now.open_questions: Can policy gaps close by 2030 to keep 1.5 C in reach? What roles will carbon removal and adaptation play?

items.reflection: Climate negotiations show how scientific consensus and political action can travel at very different speeds.

moments.title: IUCN founded
moments.who: International Union for Conservation of Nature
moments.body: Founded in Fontainebleau, IUCN compiles the Red List of Threatened Species from 1964 onwards.
moments.takeaway: Conservation governance began as an inter-state and NGO initiative.

moments.title: Convention on Biological Diversity
moments.body: The Convention on Biological Diversity opens for signature, committing parties to biodiversity conservation, sustainable use and equitable benefit-sharing.
moments.takeaway: Biodiversity and climate frameworks emerged from the same political moment.

moments.title: Global Biodiversity Framework
moments.body: Parties agree to protect 30% of land and sea by 2030 ('30x30').
moments.takeaway: Quantitative biodiversity targets joined climate-style numerical pledges.

now.title: Biodiversity today
now.body: Living Planet Index and IUCN Red List both indicate continuing declines. Major drivers include land-use change, climate change, pollution and invasive species.
now.open_questions: How can biodiversity finance scale to delivery? What metrics best track ecosystem function rather than species counts alone?

items.reflection: Biodiversity policy has historically received less attention than climate; the two are increasingly treated as joined problems.
